 SUBJECT:  Bear Electrical Solutions – Amendment No. 1

RECOMMENDATION:

It is recommended that the City Council consider:
  1. Authorize the City Manager to execute the First Amendment to Agreement 2183-
  A, in a form approved by the City Attorney, with Bear Electrical Solutions, Inc., to
  retroactively increase the contract amount not to exceed $668,000 and to extend
  the term through June 30, 2024; and
  2. Taking such additional, related action that may be desirable.
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:

The City’s traffic signal maintenance contract expires on June 30, 2023. Staff
recommends exercising the City’s option to extend for an additional one-year term (July
1, 2023- June 30, 3024) with a revised contract amount of $668,000. The increased
contract amount would cover maintenance services for FY23-24 and increased
expenditures for the current fiscal year. As part of its traffic signal maintenance plan, the
City anticipates a certain volume of call-outs. However, the City experienced an increased
need for extraordinary, non-routine, maintenance during the 2022-23 fiscal year due to a
high number of call-outs related to traffic accidents, damage to equipment, weather, and
equipment malfunctions.

BACKGROUND:

The City of Monterey Park owns and operates 60 traffic signals and five pedestrian
flashing beacons. The City’s traffic signal maintenance contract involves “routine”
preventative maintenance and “extraordinary” maintenance. Routine maintenance is
monthly inspection of the traffic signal equipment at all 60 locations and five pedestrian
flashing beacons, and includes reviewing the signal timing and operation, and performing
repairs as necessary. Extraordinary maintenance involves service call-outs of equipment
failure or malfunction of the signal system whether caused by vehicle collision, vandalism,
civil disorder, or natural disasters.

In September 2020, the City entered into Agreement 2183-A with Bear Electrical
Solutions for a three-year term and a not to exceed amount of $324,000 for traffic signal
maintenance. The Agreement is set to expire on June 30, 2023. Bear Electrical is highly
qualified to perform traffic signal maintenance work and provided great service during the
term of the contract. They have also provided valuable support to the City for ongoing
traffic signal improvement projects.

Staff recommends amending the agreement to extend the term for one additional year
and to update the rate schedule (Attachment 1) as allowed by the contract. Due to an
increased need for extraordinary maintenance, it is also recommended that the City
increase the contract amount to $668,000. The revised amount would cover increased
expenditures for FY 22-23 and the estimated costs for FY 23-24. The estimated cost for
traffic signal maintenance for FY 23-24 is $205,000. This includes routine preventative
maintenance and extraordinary maintenance and response due to service call-outs.

FISCAL IMPACT:

During FY 22-23, the City experienced an increased need for extraordinary, non-routine,
maintenance during the year due to a high number of call-outs related to traffic accidents,
damage to equipment, weather, and equipment malfunctions. The City will be using
budgeted unexpended General Funds to cover the increased expenditures for these call-
outs. Traffic signal maintenance is generally funded by the General Fund and Gas Tax
Fund. The City will attempt to recover costs for call-outs related to damage as a result of
a traffic collision.

 SUBJECT:  Southern California Edison 5-year Revocable Secondary Land Use
  License

RECOMMENDATION:

It is recommended that the City Council consider:
  1. Authorizing the City Manager to execute a 5-year Revocable Secondary Land Use
  License with Southern California Edison (SCE) for the City’s 14” water main from
  the Delta Water Treatment Plant in the amount of $1,934.08; and
  2. Taking such additional, related action that may be desirable.
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:

The City of Monterey Park owns and operates a 14” water main line that provides water
to the City of Monterey Park residents and businesses which falls within Southern
California Edison (SCE) property. A new 5-year Revocable Secondary Land Use License
(License) is needed to allow the City to continue to operate the 14” water main line within
the SCE property. Staff is recommending approval of the License.

BACKGROUND:

The City of Monterey Park owns and operates the Delta Water Treatment Plant located
in the City of Rosemead. Water is conveyed through a 14” water main line from this
location to the City of Monterey Park and provides water to residents and businesses
through an SCE property.

In 2018, the City re-lined the 14” water main line which required the City to enter into
License Agreement 2091-AB with SCE. The existing License was for a term of five years
and allows for extensions. With the original 5-year license coming to an end, it is
recommended that the City renew the license to continue the use of the 14” water main
line.

Staff has reviewed the License and recommends approval.

FISCAL IMPACT:

The total cost for the 5-year Revocable Secondary Land Use License is $1,934.08.
Funding for this License is available in the Water funds (401).

  36. Electric and Magnetic Fields (“EMF”): There are numerous sources of power frequency
electric and magnetic field (“EMF”), including household or building wiring, electrical appliances and
electric power transmission and distribution facilities. There have been numerous scientific studies
about the potential health effects of EMF. Interest in a potential link between long-term exposures to
EMF and certain diseases is based on this scientific research and public concerns.

While some 40 years of research have not established EMF as a health hazard, some health authorities
have identified magnetic field exposures as a possible human carcinogen. Many of the questions about
diseases have been successfully resolved due to an aggressive international research program. However,
potentially important public health questions remain about whether there is a link between EMF
exposures in homes or work and some diseases including childhood leukemia and a variety of other
adult diseases (e.g. adult cancers and miscarriages). While scientific research is continuing on a wide
range of questions relating to exposures at both work and in our communities, a quick resolution of the
remaining scientific uncertainties is not expected.

Since Licensee plans to license or otherwise enter Licensor property that is in close proximity to Licensor
electric facilities, Licensor wants to share with Licensee and those who may enter the property under
this agreement, the information available about EMF. Accordingly, Licensor has attached to this
document a brochure that explains some basic facts about EMF and that describes Licensor policy on
EMF. Licensor also encourages Licensee to obtain other information as needed to assist in
understanding the EMF regarding the planned use of this property.

 SUBJECT:  Receive and File Staff Report Summarizing the Status of Emergency
  Repairs of the Monterey Pass Road Water Line

RECOMMENDATION:
It is recommended that the City Council consider:
  1. Receive and File the staff report summarizing the status of emergency repairs of
  the Monterey Pass Road water line; and
  2. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

BACKGROUND:
On August 17, 2022, City Council adopted Resolution No. 2022-R69 authorizing the City
Manager to take necessary measures for emergency repair of a water main line on
Monterey Pass Road. Recurring water main leaks in several areas within Monterey Pass
Road between the intersections of Vagabond Drive and Brightwood street resulted in
extensive infrastructure damage to the roadway and necessary water main pipe repairs
to ensure continued water service to residences and businesses in the area.

The design phase was completed in December 2022 followed by research of available
material and cost during the months of December and January to ensure the project could
be expedited due to the significant material delivery delays. Construction started on
March 2023 and is scheduled to be complete by October 2023.

As part of the City’s outreach efforts, the construction manager visited business along the
project area prior to the start of the project to notify them of the upcoming construction.
The Economic Development Division also mailed out letters to businesses that may be
impacted by this project. Message boards were placed within the project area prior to
construction commencing to alert drivers of the impact to their commutes. The City will
continue to provide project updates to the community for the duration of the project
through the City website, social media, and City Council meetings. A dedicated webpage
has been established on the city’s website as, www.Montereypark.ca.gov/Montereypass,
to inform the public about the project and provide progress updates. Residents and
businesses can also sign up to receive project updates by subscribing to NIXLE, by
texting "MPSS" to 888777.

RECOMMENDATION:
It is recommended that the City Council consider:
  1. Opening a public hearing to receive documentary and testimonial evidence;
  2. After closing the public hearing and considering the evidence, adopting a
  Resolution finding the FY2023-24 Capital Improvement Plan (“CIP”) conforms with
  the General Plan, Authorizing the City Engineer to Approve Plans and
  Specifications for Capital Improvement Projects, and Authorizing the Public Works
  Director to Solicit Bids for Capital Improvement Projects identified in the CIP; and
  3. Take such additional, related action that may be desirable.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The City’s FY2023-24 proposed budget includes an updated Capital Improvement Plan
(“CIP”) outlining the City’s capital investments over a five-year period. Staff seeks the City
Council’s adoption of a Resolution to approve the proposed CIP, grant authorization for
the City Engineer to approve plans specifications for Capital Improvement Projects and
authorization for the Director of Public Works to advertise projects for construction bids
when required or needed.

BACKGROUND
The CIP generally identifies which capital improvement projects will be built during a five-
year period; it is updated annually and approved by the City Council. The CIP includes
major enhancements and repairs to critical public assets, including parks, City-owned
facilities, streets, traffic signals, storm drains, sidewalks, bus stops, transportation, water
and sewer facilities. Completion of CIP projects helps to enhance the overall quality of life
in the City by improving the physical structures, systems, and facilities that provide
services to the community. The Public Works Department is responsible for implementing
the City’s CIP. Each year, Public Works, in conjunction with other Departments, reviews
the City’s capital needs and prioritizes projects through the annual budget process.

It is recommended that the City Council adopt a resolution approving the proposed FY
2023-24 CIP list of projects. If the proposed Resolution is adopted, the CIP will be
approved; the City Engineer will be authorized to approve plans/specifications (for design
immunity purposes); and the Public Works Director will be authorized to solicit bids for
CIP projects.

  MINUTES
  MONTEREY PARK CITY COUNCIL
  FINANCING AUTHORITY (MPFA)
  HOUSING AUTHORITY (MPHA)
  GEOLOGIC HAZARD ABATEMENT DISTRICT (GHAD)
  SUCCESSOR AGENCY (SA)
  REGULAR MEETING
  JUNE 21, 2023

The City Council, the Financing Authority (MPFA), the Housing Authority (MPHA), the
Geologic Hazard Abatement District (GHAD), and the Successor Agency (SA) of the City
of Monterey Park held a Regular Meeting of the Council in the Council Chamber, located
at 320 West Newmark Avenue in the City of Monterey Park, Wednesday, June 21, 2023
at 6:30 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER:
Mayor Sanchez called the meeting to order at 6:37 p.m.

FLAG SALUTE:
The Police Explorers called the flag salute.

ROLL CALL:
City Clerk Maychelle Yee called the roll:

Council Members Present:  Vinh Ngo, Jose Sanchez, Thomas Wong, Yvonne Yiu
Council Members Absent:  Henry Lo

ALSO PRESENT: City Treasure Amy Lee, City Manager Ron Bow, City Attorney Karl
Berger, Assistant City Manager Inez Alvarez, City Librarian Diana Garcia, Director of
Public Works Shawn Igoe, Director of Recreation and Community Services Robert
Aguirre, Director of Finance Martha Garcia, Community Development Director Jessica
Serrano, Director of Human Resources and Risk Manager Christine Tomikawa, Police
Captain Gus Jimenez, Police Captain Bill Cuevas, Fire Captain Justin Birrell, Fire Marshal
Jessica Estrella, Traffic Bureau Commander Police Sergeant Peter Yung, Police
Sergeant Randy Esparza, Corporal Izzy Flores, Finance Manager Laura Borjon, Senior
Planner Beth Chow, Program Coordinator Alejandra Espinosa, Deputy City Clerk Cindy
Trang

VIRTUALLY PRESENT: Police Chief Scott Wiese, Fire Chief Matt Hallock

AGENDA ADDITIONS, DELETIONS, CHANGES AND ADOPTIONS
City Attorney Berger announced that the City Council will adjourn to the June 21, 2023
5:00 p.m. Special Meeting Closed Session at the conclusion of this Regular Meeting.

  MISSION STATEMENT
  The mission of the City of Monterey Park is to provide excellent services to enhance
  the quality of life for our entire community.
   71-174
  June 21, 2023
PUBLIC COMMUNICATIONS

  - City Clerk Yee received, filed, and read into the record a written communication
  from Jose Mendivil requesting for support of the Service Employees International
  Union (SEIU) contract.

  - Jesus Hernandez, Chapter President of Service Employees International Union
  (SEIU) 721, expressed concerns in the City’s delay response for data and the
  sudden urgency to reach an agreement. He said SEIU is dealing in good faith
  and is seeking for a fair labor agreement.

  - Lauren Frazier, Chapter Vice President of SEIU 721, read into the record letters
  from library staff Megan Munger and Madelinn Ornelas, seeking support from the
  City Council to take the proposal seriously and consideration of fair wages.

  - Bill Lam encouraged ridership on the Metro Rail and Busway with its 2 new lines
  and expressed happiness about the extension of the City’s Spirit bus hours. He
  expressed concerns about the lack of transit service commuting north and south
  on Monterey Pass Road.

  - Daniel Martinez gave his time to Lorraine Martinez.

  - Maychelle Yee, resident, gave her time to Lorraine Martinez.

  - Lorraine Martinez stated that the decision from the last meeting for the placement
  of the Asian American Pacific Islander (AAPI) mural is inappropriate for George
  Elder Park as it encroaches on the building named in honor of Officer George
  Elder. She suggested as resolution, to imprint the artwork onto large street
  banners and hang the banners across major intersections, in recognition of AAPI
  Heritage Month and use the Elder Park location to depict heroes honoring the
  City’s Police and Fire departments.

STAFF COMMUNICATIONS

  - Fire Department: Fire Marshal Jessica Estrella reminded the community of fire
  safety including the use of safe and sane fireworks and reiterated fines for use
  of illegal fireworks. Captain Justin Birrell spoke of the citywide automated
  external defibrillator (AED) program since 2008 which save lives by providing
  early shock therapy to stimulate the beating of the heart and encouraged the
  community to engage in the Community Emergency Response Team (CERT)
  program.

  - Police Department: Captain Gus Jimenez invited the community to the Annual
  National Night Out event on August 1. Sergeant Yung provided an overview of
  the Traffic Safety Programs and spoke of several traffic grants the City received.
  Sergeant Espinoza and Corporal Flores gave an update on the Neighborhood
   71-175
  June 21, 2023
  Engagement Team (NET) program and provided the statistic on the
  homelessness count and mental health calls. Mayor Pro Tem Wong directed staff
  to seek Council’s assistance if there is a need to seek additional resources from
  other agencies.

  - Public Works: Director of Public Works Igoe reported the restoration of the Spirit
  Bus Route 5, the extension of bus hours to 6:30 a.m. – 6:30 p.m., and the Passio
  GO! App which provides bus real time data and updates.

  - Recreation and Community Services Department: Director of Recreation and
  Community Service Aguirre recited some of the past events and thanked the
  community for their support. He announced the sold out MPK Night at Dodger
  Stadium event and also thanked City Attorney Berger and his law firm with their
  sponsorship of 41 residents through an annual trust honoring the Late Mayor Pro
  Tem Fred Sornoso. Program Coordinator Espinosa invited the community to the
  following upcoming events and programs: Movie in the Park featuring Disney’s
  Lightyear on June 22 at Barnes Park, Independence Day Celebration on July 1
  at Barnes Park, summer pool schedule, and the summer lunch program at
  Barnes.

1.  PRESENTATION
  Matters listed under presentation are informational content and for discussion only.

1-A.  LOS ANGELES AREA REGIONAL TRAINING GROUP - VIDEO: FIRST
  RESPONDER PERSPECTIVES OF THE JANUARY 21, 2023 MASS SHOOTING

  Fire Chief Hallock, on behalf of the City and the Fire Department, expressed their
  most sincere sympathy to all those that had their lives altered in this tragedy. He
  summarized a training opportunity regarding the need to provide mental health for
  first responders and presented a video that provides firsthand accounts from the
  first responders on the night of the tragedy.

2.  OLD BUSINESS
  None.

3.  CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS NOS. 3A-3L

  All items under the Consent Calendar are considered by the City Council to be
  routine and will be enacted by one motion. Specific items may be removed from
  the Consent Calendar at the request of any member of the City Council for
  separate consideration.

  Action Taken: Mayor Sanchez announced that Council Member Lo missed the
  council meeting because he is on his way back from a trip to Washington D.C.
  Council Member Ngo declared a potential conflict of interest as he serves as a
  Board Member on Chinatown Service Center and did not participate on Agenda
   71-176
  June 21, 2023
  Item No. 3H. Mayor Pro Tem Wong declared a potential conflict of interest as his
  employer, Southern California Edison, is the subject for discussion and did not
  participate on Agenda Item No. 3K.

  The City Council approved and adopted Agenda Item Nos. 3A, 3B, 3C, 3D, 3F,
  3G, 3H, 3I, 3J, 3K and 3L on Consent Calendar, excluding Item No. 3E which was
  pulled for discussion, separate motion, reading resolutions and ordinances by the
  title only and waiving further reading thereof.

  Motion: Moved by Mayor Pro Tem Wong and seconded by Council Member Yiu,
  motion carried by the following vote:

  Ayes:  Council Members:  Lo, Yiu, Ngo, Wong, Sanchez
  Noes:  Council Members:  None
  Absent:  Council Members:  None
  Abstain:  Council Members:  None

3-A.  MONTHLY INVESTMENT REPORT – MAY 2023

  As of May 31, 2023, invested funds for the City of Monterey Park is
  $87,846,698.82.

  Action Taken: The City Council received and filed the monthly investment report,
  on Consent Calendar.

3-B.  RECOMMENDATIONS FOR ADOPTION OF FISCAL YEAR 2023-24 ANNUAL
  BUDGET

  On May 24, 2023, the City Council conducted a public budget workshop regarding
  the City’s current finances, projected revenues, and financial obligations. The
  budget for FY 2023-2024 presents a spending plan that anticipates $145.5 million
  in estimated operating revenues and transfers-in; $27.5 million from grant
  advancements and fund balance from all funds combined; and $173 million in
  operating, and capital improvements expenditures and transfers-out. Financial
  matters, included the addition of staff, the American Rescue Program Act funds,
  Community Development Department projects, the Citywide compensation study,
  and all other goals and objectives associated with the City budget, were presented
  and discussed at the workshop.

  In addition, the City Council’s fiscal year 2023-2024 Strategic Plan Goals were
  added to the budget document to provide a roadmap for prioritizing implementation
  of the specific objectives that will be focused on during the budget cycle.
   71-177
  June 21, 2023
  Action Taken: The City Council adopted Resolution No. 2023-R48 / SA-186
  adopting the City’s and Successor Agency’s Fiscal Year 2023-2024 Annual Budget
  as presented on May 24, 2023; and adopted Resolution No. 2023-R49 approving
  the Citywide Combined Salary Schedule, on Consent Calendar.

3-C.  CONTINUE TO EXTEND THE EXISTENCE OF  AN  EMPLOYMENT
  EMERGENCY FOR THE CITY OF MONTEREY PARK

  The City continues to make progress on filling vacancies. Since April 2023, the
  City has hired or promoted candidates to fill Public Works Maintenance Supervisor,
  two Financial Analysts, Recreation Manager, Code Enforcement Officer, two
  Police Officers, and an Economic Development Specialist.

  There are 30 full-time positions in the recruitment process along with 18 part-time
  recruitments. Staff recommends extending the employment emergency as the City
  is in the process of revising the Personnel Rules and Regulations to assist with
  modifying the recruitment processes and procedures and recruiting qualified
  candidates to fill the Water division vacancies continues to be challenging in the
  current workforce market.

  Action Taken: The City Council received and filed the staff report; and continued

3-E.  AUTHORIZING MAYOR TO SIGN LETTERS ON BEHALF OF THE CITY
  SUPPORTING GOVERNOR NEWSOM’S PROPOSAL FOR A 28TH
  AMENDMENT TO THE UNITED STATES CONSTITUTION AND THE
  LANGUAGE ACCESS TO GUN VIOLENCE PREVENTION STRATEGIES ACT
  OF 2023; AND RECEIVING AND FILING THE FIREARM LEGISLATIVE
  UPDATE REPORT

  On January 21, 2023, the City of Monterey Park experienced a Mass Casualty
  Incident (MCI) where 20 people were shot. Eleven of those community members
  died. As our community struggles with the challenge of working through this
  tragedy, fellow citizens and residents in California and the rest of the country
  continue to be confronted with substantially similar MCIs.

  State and federal legislation continues to be proposed to help reduce the likelihood
  that other communities will suffer the same fate as Monterey Park and numerous
  other communities across the United States.

  As requested by City Council Members, it is recommended that the City Council
  consider supporting Governor Newsom’s proposal for a 28th Amendment to the
  United States Constitution to help address America’s gun violence crisis and
  supporting the Language Access to Gun Violence Prevention Strategies Act of
  2023.
   71-179
  June 21, 2023
  Staff recommends City Council receive and file the firearm legislative update
  report.

  Action Taken: The City Council (1) authorized the Mayor to sign a letter on behalf
  of the City supporting Governor Newsom’s proposal for a 28th Amendment to the
  United States Constitution to help address America’s Gun Violence Crisis; (2)
  authorized the Mayor to sign a letter on behalf of the City supporting the Language
  Access to Gun Violence Prevention Strategies Act of 2023; and (3) received and
  filed the firearm legislative update report, as amended to make the letters a 5
  signature letter.

3-F.  WAIVE FURTHER READING AND ADOPT ZONING CODE AMENDMENT NO.
  23-01 (ZCA-23-01), AN ORDINANCE AMENDING THE MONTEREY PARK
  MUNICIPAL CODE, CHAPTER 21.18, ENTITLED “AFFORDABLE HOUSING
  INCENTIVES – DENSITY BONUS” TO IMPLEMENT THE MONTEREY PARK
  HOUSING ELEMENT

  In March of 2022, the City Council categorized an update of the Density Bonus
  Ordinance as a moderate priority. On November 2, 2022, City Council asked Staff
  to bring forward an update to the Density Bonus Ordinance in coordination with the
  Inclusionary Housing Ordinance. On November 16, 2022, the City Council
  amended and adopted the 2021-2029 Housing Element that included Program 14:
  Affordable Housing Development Incentives, which identified an objective to
  consider updating the City’s Density Ordinance.

  A density bonus is an incentive-based tool that permits a developer to increase the
  maximum allowable development density on a site in exchange for specified public
  policy goals. If adopted, the proposed Ordinance would provide density bonuses
  to help develop affordable housing units in exchange for a menu of incentives to
  make development easier. This is accomplished by reducing the applicable
  development standards such as height, floor area ratio, and setbacks, among
  others.

  Density bonus regulations are mandated by Government Code § 65915. The City’s
  density bonus regulations were last updated in 2013 and there have been changes
  in California law during the last ten years that require amendments to the MPMC.
  The proposed Ordinance will reconcile the City’s regulations with applicable law.
   71-180
  June 21, 2023

  Action Taken: The City Council waived the second reading and adopted
  Ordinance No. 2230, on Consent Calendar.

3-G.  WAIVE FURTHER READING AND ADOPT ORDINANCES: 1) ZONE CHANGE
  (ZA-23-01) TO RE-ZONE PROPERTIES FROM THE REGIONAL SPECIALTY
  CENTER (R-S) ZONE WITH THE PLANNED DEVELOPMENT OVERLAY (P-D)
  ZONE TO THE MARKET PLACE SPECIFIC PLAN (MPSP) ZONE; AND 2)
  DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT (DA-23-01) TO AMEND IN ITS ENTIRETY A
  DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT BETWEEN MONTEREY PARK RETAIL
  PARTNERS, LLC AND THE CITY OF MONTEREY PARK FOR PROPERTIES
  COLLECTIVELY OPERATING AS THE MONTEREY PARK MARKET PLACE,
  LOCATED AT 2000-5500 MARKET PLACE DRIVE, ALSO IDENTIFIED BY
  ASSESSOR’S PARCEL NUMBERS 5275-003-024, 025, 027, 029, 030, 031, 037,
  AND 038

  The Monterey Park Market Place development was originally approved through a
  Precise Plan (PP-12-01) that was intended to redevelop a brownfield site to help
  stimulate the local economy and create jobs while preserving the environment and
  public safety of the area. Since the creation and implementation of PP-12-01,
  Phase 1 is complete, but Phases 2 and 3 remain unbuilt. Phase 2 includes the
  wrap-around road south of the Leachate Treatment Plant (LTP) and Thermal
  Destruction Facility (TDF), and Phase 3 is the built-out of the area west of the
  LTP/TDF.

  In recent years, market forces changed the way in which consumers conduct
  business: a decreased need for traditional brick-and-mortar stores and an
  increased demand for last mile facilities, warehouses, auto dealerships, and sound
  stages for the entertainment industry emerged since the beginning of the COVID-
  19 pandemic. The applicant seeks to create flexibility to allow for land uses that
  help address the changing landscape of the commercial/service sector by
  providing a framework through the proposed Market Place Specific Plan (“MPSP”)
  to allow for such uses. No immediate construction or development is proposed at
  this time.

  The Project includes the proposed adoption of the MPSP to address the eventual
  build-out of the Market Place; it supersedes the existing Precise Plan. The Specific
  Plan will be identified within the Monterey Park Municipal Code (“MPMC”) and the
  entire Market Place Project site will be re-zoned from the Regional Specialty
  Center with Planned Development Overlay, to the MPSP. Further, the amended
  and restated Development agreement between the City and the Applicant will help
   71-181
  June 21, 2023
 ensure that the eventual build-out of the Market Place will provide a public benefit
 to the community.

 Most recently, the City Council considered a similar proposal of the site that was
 not approved at its April 19, 2023 meeting. Following that date, on May 15, 2023,
 the applicant submitted a new application. That application includes a revised
 Specific Plan that includes new uses that would be permitted at the site for
 additional Council consideration.

 Public Comment:

- Maychelle Yee, resident, said she is speaking on behalf of her neighbors Cole
  SooHoo, Brandon Drake, Darin Furukawa, Hailey Lee, B Wu, Peter Castanon, and
  Tammy Sam expressing concerns with the traffic situation, parking, vehicular
  circulation and the ingress/egress of traffic flow. She suggested presenting this
  item to the Planning Commission for recommendations before rehearing this item.

- Dale Goldsmith, Armbruster Golsmith & Delvac LLP, Attorney at Law, representing
  the applicant, explained efforts to address traffic safety and to improve traffic flow
  by rerouting traffic and allowing for a new entrance from Market Place Drive. He
  added that the specific plan supports phrase 3 which includes a new travel lane to
  provide for a more direct route to the Costco gas station.

 Action Taken: The City Council waived the second reading and adopted
 Ordinance No. 2031, Zone Change and Ordinance No. 2032, Development
 Agreement, on Consent Calendar.

3-H.  AUTHORIZE THE CITY MANAGER TO EXECUTE A LICENSE AGREEMENT
  WITH CHINATOWN SERVICE CENTER TO UTILIZE THE SIERRA VISTA
  COMMUNITY CENTER AS A TEMPORARY MPK HOPE RESILIENCY CENTER
  TO PROVIDE MENTAL HEALTH AND WELLNESS SERVICES IN THE WAKE
  OF THE JANUARY 21ST SHOOTING

  Beginning in January 2023 Chinatown Service Center (CSC) spearheaded the
  efforts to assist with the mental health and wellness of community members
  following the January 21, 2023 mass shooting at the Star Ballroom dance studio.

  In March 2023 Chinatown Service Center was invited to apply for the Antiterrorism
  Emergency Assistance Program (AEAP) grant from the Federal Office for Victims
  of Crime (OVC) to fund the establishment of a Community Resiliency Center to
  serve the victims and community members affected by the incident. This grant
  guarantees Resiliency Center funding to affected communities, however
  disbursement is not immediate, and it can take up to 18 months for agencies to
  receive funds.

  Chinatown Service Center is seeking a location for a temporary Community
  Resiliency Center while they work on identifying a permanent location. City staff
  have worked with CSC to find potential City facilities to house a temporary
  Community Resiliency Center and have identified the Sierra Vista Community
  Center as a site.

  The City would like to execute a license agreement with Chinatown Service Center
  for use of the Sierra Vista Community Center until December 31, 2023. As part of
  the license agreement, the City will provide the space for Chinatown Service
  Center to provide individual and group therapy, wellness activities, tai chi and
  meditation and other activities for the community.

  Staff is recommending City Council authorize the City Manager, or designee, to
  execute a license agreement, in a form approved by the City Attorney, to use the
  Sierra Vista Community Center to provide a temporary Community Resiliency
  Center.

  Public Comments:

  - Peter Ng, CEO of Chinatown Service Center, spoke about the importance of
  working together and requested the City Council consider granting Chinatown

  EMERGENCY REPAIRS OF THE MONTEREY PASS ROAD WATER LINE

  On August 17, 2022, City Council adopted Resolution No. 2022-R69 authorizing
  the City Manager to take necessary measures for emergency repair of a water
  main line on Monterey Pass Road. Recurring water main leaks in several areas
  within Monterey Pass Road between the intersections of Vagabond Drive and
  Brightwood street resulted in extensive infrastructure damage to the roadway and
  necessary water main pipe repairs to ensure continued water service to residences
  and businesses in the area.
   71-185
  June 21, 2023
  As of the week ending on June 16, the contractor will have completed
  approximately 69% of the project with the installation of 7,500 linear feet of 12”
  PVC water pipeline along Monterey Pass between Floral Dr and Vagabond
  Rd. Traffic control devices have provided a safe working condition for both
  contractor and the driving public. These devices are removed at the end of the day
  and proper temporary asphalt resurfacing of the trench has provided a seamless
  transition for vehicular traffic. Street sweeping is performed on a daily basis to
